title: Containerd process loads one of CPU cores up to 100%
body:
### Description

Recently I noticed containerd process starts to load one of CPU cores up to 100%, like a busy loop. I haven't figured out yet what triggers this behavior. It was observed two times in last three days.
Containerd in my system is installed as a dependency for docker package. Currently I have no any containers running and even no docker images registered.

Log from containerd service with golang stack dump: [containerd.log.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20084245/containerd.log.gz)

Note CPU load started a couple of hours later after "containerd successfully booted in 0.201601s". I noticed it by fan noise increase as a response to CPU temperature increase.

CPU load calmed down after I attached to the containerd process with gdb and then exited. 
(Nothing suspicious found there, one thread was in `epoll_wait()`, all others in `futexsleep()`).

I already installed containerd debug info package and will try to get more information as soon as it goes crazy again.

System: Arch Linux x86_64, kernel 6.14.5-arch1-1.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

_No response_

### Describe the results you received and expected

Containerd process should not consume 100% of CPU core for a long time when idle.

### What version of containerd are you using?

containerd github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.0.5 fb4c30d4ede3531652d86197bf3fc9515e5276d9.m

### Any other relevant information

_No response_

### Show configuration if it is related to CRI plugin.

_No response_

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Adding another data point — this reproduces reliably (not just on idle) on **ARM64 / Raspberry Pi 5**, so it doesn't seem to be x86_64/Arch-specific.
**System:**
- Raspberry Pi 5, Debian 13 (Trixie)
- Kernel: 6.18.34+rpt-rpi-v8 (arm64)
- Docker Engine: 29.6.2
- containerd: v2.2.6
- runc: 1.3.6
- /var/lib/docker on local NVMe SSD (ext4), not network storage

**Trigger**: In my case this is 100% reproducible on demand, not just spontaneous. dockerd pegs one core to 100% as soon as I try to view a container's logs — both through Portainer's web UI log viewer and directly via docker logs / docker logs -f on the CLI. Happens with every container, not just specific ones. Log files themselves are small (log rotation active, max-size 10m).
**Workaround**: sudo systemctl restart docker resolves it temporarily — after restarting, docker logs works fine again until the next trigger.
strace -p $(pidof dockerd) -f -tt -c while the CPU was pegged (summary):

% time     seconds  usecs/call     calls    errors syscall
 59.31    4.295596        2221      1934       211 futex
 16.92    1.225666         633      1936           epoll_pwait
 15.05    1.089763          22     47847           nanosleep
  7.26    0.525562           1    340263           pread64
  0.50    0.036570        4571         8           waitid
  0.18    0.013126          10      1211       382 read
  0.12    0.008911          27       322        57 openat
  0.10    0.006964         120        58           getpid
  0.08    0.006115           8       721           readlinkat
  0.07    0.004935           5       938         6 fcntl
  0.06    0.004567          11       413         1 write

Notably high pread64 count as well, alongside the futex/epoll_pwait/nanosleep pattern already reported here.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
Did some further profiling on this (Raspberry Pi 5, kernel 6.18.34, Docker 29.6.2, containerd 2.2.6). A few findings that point away from the eventpoll timeout theory suggested above:

Kernel is well past the window where 0a65bc27bd64/d9ec733 were introduced/fixed (~6.14.4–6.14.8, mid-2025), so the fix should already be included here.
On-CPU stack sampling (bpftrace, 99Hz) during an active spike shows no eventpoll/epoll frames at all — the hot stacks are pread64 → ext4_file_read_iter/vfs_read, plus a large volume of very short, hard-to-sample syscalls. nanosleep calls outnumber epoll_pwait roughly 15-25:1, which doesn't match a 1:1 epoll-timeout spin pattern.
inotify limits are nowhere near exhausted (41/128 instances).

Current working hypothesis: this looks more like dockerd's own pkg/filenotify polling fallback getting stuck in a tight retry loop, possibly related to the known log-rotation race (moby/moby#37646) rather than a containerd/kernel-level issue. Log rotation is active on this system (max-size: 10m).

Currently running a small watchdog that auto-triggers diagnostics (log-rotation timestamps, strace summary, a timing test against a quiescent container's log file) the moment CPU spikes, to catch the next occurrence with better data. Will report back once we have a clean sample.
